lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Application or project: food safety, storage, and reheating

objective: With a trusted adult, learners check three real items in the refrigerator or pantry against provided safe-temperature and shelf-life guidelines, sort each as safe to keep or needing attention, and correctly reheat one real food item to a safe internal temperature or visible doneness sign confirmed by the adult, so they can recognize and prevent foodborne illness risk at home.
scenario: With a trusted adult present, the learner selects three real items from the household refrigerator or pantry, checks each against the provided safe-storage guidelines (such as refrigerator temperature range and typical shelf-life windows), and records whether each item is still safe. The learner then reheats one real leftover or refrigerated item using a safe method from the guidance sheet, and the adult confirms the item was heated appropriately before the task counts as complete.
safetyNotes: The learner only handles the stove, microwave, or oven for reheating with the trusted adult present the entire time.
If an item shows signs of spoilage such as an off smell, mold, or an expired shelf-life window, the learner does not taste it; the adult decides whether to discard it.
Completing this task sheet never certifies the safety check or reheating by itself; a guardian confirmation is required before the task counts as complete.

simulationAlternative.description: If a real refrigerator or pantry check and reheating session is not possible, the learner instead works from a provided list of ten food items with their storage location and age, sorts each into 'safe to keep' or 'needs attention' using the same safe-storage guidelines, and separately identifies the correct reheating method and target temperature or doneness sign for two of the listed items, explaining the reasoning for each choice.

materials: access to the real household refrigerator or pantry with a trusted adult
the provided safe-temperature and shelf-life guidance sheet
a real food item to reheat and a safe way to reheat it (stove, microwave, or oven)
paper or a notes app to record findings

tasks.directions: Before checking, predict which of three items you plan to check might already be past its safe window.

prompts.text: Name the three items you plan to check and write your prediction for whether each is still safe, based only on what you remember about when it was stored.

tasks.directions: With your adult, check each of the three items against the guidance sheet's temperature and shelf-life information, and record the result for each.

prompts.text: I checked item one against the guidance sheet and recorded whether it is safe to keep or needs attention.
I checked item two against the guidance sheet and recorded whether it is safe to keep or needs attention.
I checked item three against the guidance sheet and recorded whether it is safe to keep or needs attention.

tasks.directions: With your adult present, choose one real food item to reheat and use the guidance sheet's method to reheat it to a safe internal temperature or visible doneness sign, then have your adult confirm the result.

prompts.text: Name the item you reheated, the method you used, and the target temperature or doneness sign from the guidance sheet.
My adult confirmed the item reached the safe target before I finished the task.

tasks.directions: Compare your predictions from the warm-up to what you actually found.

prompts.text: Which item's condition most surprised you compared to your prediction, and explain one specific habit you will change about how you store or check food because of what you found.

remediation: If a learner sorts an item as safe based only on its smell or appearance rather than checking it against the guidance sheet's stated shelf-life window, reteach by covering the item and having them find and read aloud the specific shelf-life range from the guidance sheet before making the safe or needs-attention call again.
extension: Have the learner check three additional pantry items against the guidance sheet's shelf-life information and create a short written schedule noting which one they should recheck first and why, based on how close it is to its safe window's end.
